Subject: AWS Marketplace CTA experimentation & onboarding handoff

Hi Sara + AWS Listings team,

Following up from our sync last week — Acme Analytics is ready to iterate on CTA experimentation and the onboarding flow for their AWS Marketplace product page. Attached are two things to start: a short PDF with three CTA variants (primary/secondary placements + microcopy) and a proposed listing copy draft. Key asks: 

- Can the Marketplace team enable A/B testing on the hero CTA for the next 30 days? We want to test: Get started (default), Try a 14-day trial, and Request a demo.
- Confirm which SKUs and billing labels support a private-offer flow for Acme (they are planning a reserved capacity SKU for enterprise customers).
- Any constraints on CTA placement or character limits for hero/subhead? We kept options concise but want to avoid truncation.

Attachments: cta-mockups-v2.pdf, proposed-listing-copy-v1.docx

Next steps: If we can get confirmation on testing availability and SKU mapping today, Marissa will push the revised copy and a short onboarding checklist for first-time users to the Drive link. Ben — can you scope how we’ll measure the lift (baseline conversion metric + expected sample size)?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

redwood.com

Hi Tessa / Sara —

Thanks for the materials. Quick clarifying questions before we enable any A/B experiments on the product page: 

1) SKU mapping: For private-offer support we need the exact Seller SKU(s) tied to the AMI/AMI alias. Can you confirm the SKU IDs?
2) Billing label: Is Acme planning to route metered billing through a single SKU or multiple SKUs for trial vs reserved? We need to know for how the CTA funnels to the correct checkout path.
3) CTA constraints: hero text limit is 45 characters; subhead up to 140 characters. We can place a secondary CTA beneath the hero but cannot have more than two primary CTAs in the hero region due to responsive layout.

We can enable A/B testing, but we need the final copy and SKU mapping before EOD tomorrow to schedule the test start early next week. Also, please provide a public-facing privacy link (or confirm we should point to Acme’s privacy page).

Best,
Liam Harper
AWS Marketplace Listings

Thanks Liam — answering inline below and attaching the updated copy doc.

1) SKU mapping: Acme will use two SKUs for launch — ACME-ENTERPRISE-RES (reserved monthly commit) and ACME-TRIAL-MET (metered trial). Sara, confirming SKU IDs: will you provide the Seller SKU numeric IDs by EOD? Those are in your seller console.

2) Billing label/flow: Plan is to have the hero CTA route to a private-offer checkout for enterprise leads (ACME-ENTERPRISE-RES). Trial CTA should route to the meter-based trial SKU (ACME-TRIAL-MET) and create a trial entitlement. We recommend the hero default be the demo/request flow for enterprise buyers and the secondary CTA be Try 14-day trial for self-service conversions.

3) CTA constraints: noted about character limits — I trimmed the variants to stay under 45 characters for hero. See the doc for exact strings.

Measurement: Ben — we propose measuring: hero CTA CTR, conversion to private-offer request, and trial activation rate. Baseline conversion from similar listings at launch was ~3.1% (we can share the workbook). Expected sample for a detectable 20% lift is ~10k impressions over 30 days — can you confirm platform telemetry is enabled?

Attachments: proposed-listing-copy-v1.docx
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3C
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

Sara — if you can pull SKU numeric IDs and confirm the privacy link we’ll hand off to AWS. Liam — once you confirm testing window availability we’ll finalize the DocuSign if needed for the private-offer flow.

—Marissa Cole

Hi all — quick final update from our side.

Sara — thanks for confirming the numeric SKU IDs (ACME-12345 for ACME-ENTERPRISE-RES; ACME-67890 for ACME-TRIAL-MET) and the privacy link: https://acmeanalytics.com/privacy.

Liam — per Marissa’s doc (attached) we trimmed the hero variants to fit 45 chars and set the default hero CTA to Request a demo (routes to private-offer flow ACME-12345). Secondary CTA: Try 14-day trial (ACME-67890). Please schedule the A/B experiment to run for 30 days starting Monday 2026-08-17 and send confirmation of the experiment ID once created.

Ben — when you have 2 minutes can you confirm telemetry will capture hero CTA clicks and private-offer requests (we need to sync on event names so HubSpot mapping works)? Also please confirm expected sample size from Marissa’s note.
